title: Oncall Roster, Scaleback Protocol & KPI Telemetry
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures the staffing roster, scaledown/scaleback decision protocol, and the minimum KPI telemetry dashboard we need to validate a safe go-live for medium-impact releases (soft traffic ramp to 50k/day). It is intentionally pragmatic: short checklists + escalation playbook + one-page metric watchlist.

Context / scope:
- Audience: on-call product-ops, SRE on duty, release lead, and engineering owners for Hosted API and Dedicated.
- Scope: feature flags + model rollout changes (no infra-only upgrades). If model binary or infra change, run the infra-specific preflight runbook (linked in artifacts).

High-level goals:
1) Keep customer-facing latency p50 < target and p95 < targetSLO during ramp.
2) Avoid sustained error rate increases > 0.5% absolute over baseline.
3) If cost-per-1k tokens spikes > 2x baseline for 10+ mins, trigger scaleback.
4) Provide a low-friction rollback path with clear ownership.

Quick contact map:
- Release lead: Leah Thompson (pager: leah.t, slack: #rl-release-ops)
- SRE on duty: Marco Chen (pager: marco.sre)
- Product-ops oncall: Aisha Patel (pager: aisha.po)
- ML owner (model behavior): Diego Rivera (slack: @diego-ml)
- Escalation to Eng Mgr: Samir Kapoor

Launch-day schedule (sprint style):
- T-72h: Final runbook review + dry run with oncall (30m). Owner: Release lead.
- T-24h: Canary config in place, 1% traffic smoke for 2h, validate telemetry. Owner: SRE.
- T-2h: Full launch briefing (ops + eng + product). Confirm rollback button and feature-flag hook. Owner: Release lead.
- T+0-2h: Ramp 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 2h if signals green.
- T+2h-24h: Observe and maintain; incremental increases only on stable signals.

Minimum KPI telemetry (one-line descriptions for dashboard widgets):
- API token throughput (reqs/min, tokens/min) - baseline vs current (line chart).
- Latency p50/p90/p95 (overall + by route/model). Auto-alert if p95 > SLO * 1.25 for 5m.
- Error rate (5xx + model-error responses) - rolling 5m/1h. Alert if > baseline + 0.5% absolute for 5m.
- Cost per 1k tokens (estimated infra + model) - rolling 15m. Alert if > 2x baseline for 10m.
- KV cache hit ratio (hosted) - drop may indicate model misrouting or cache warming issues.
- Queue backlog (requests waiting to be batched) - alert if > X threshold per worker.
- External dependencies (DB/API) latency and error % - quick binary green/orange/red.
- User-visible degradation signals (via synthetic checks) - failures of end-to-end smoke requests.

Alert thresholds (recommendation):
- Page (immediate): p95 latency > SLO*1.5 for >5m, error rate > 2% absolute, cost-per-1k > 3x baseline for 5m, queue backlog > critical threshold.
- Notify (non-pager): p95 > SLO*1.25 for >5m, error rate > baseline + 0.5% for 10m, cost-per-1k > 2x baseline for 10m.

Scaleback protocol (decision tree in prose):
1) Detect sustained metric breach (see alerts). Duty SRE opens incident doc and marks "scaleback candidate".
2) Triage: check release-config, recent deploys, model variant routing, regional vs global. Owner: SRE on duty + ML owner.
3) Soft mitigation steps (do in order, 5-10m per step, stop if metrics recover):
   - Reduce traffic to new model variant via feature-flag (50% of its share).
   - Reduce batch sizes (temporarily) to reduce latency tail if batching causes backlog.
   - Increase autoscale target for workers if CPU saturating (quick fix).
4) If no recovery in 15m after soft steps, perform scaleback = route traffic to prior stable model variant or decrease global rollout % to 0%. Owner: Release lead + SRE.
5) If scaleback triggers, spin down new variant, document root cause hypothesis in incident doc, and schedule postmortem.

Rollback runbook (short):
- When: tangible customer impact OR inability to restore within 30m of scaleback steps.
- How: Use the feature-flag controller to revert routing to last known-good model id. If the change included infra/config that cannot be toggled, follow the infra rollback playbook (linked).
- Post-rollback steps: communicate to customers (SR team), freeze further traffic increases, tag PRs that introduced change, and open follow-up ticket with priority P1.

Readiness scoring rubric (quick 0-100):
- Code & infra: smoke tests passing (20 points) = 20 if pass, 0 if fail.
- Canary stability: 1% canary for 2h with acceptable metrics (20 points).
- Rollback validated: ability to switch routing in < 3m (15 points).
- Oncall coverage: pager + 2 backups assigned (15 points).
- Telemetry coverage: all KPI widgets in dashboard + alerts wired (15 points).
- Communication plan: support rows + customer comms prewritten (15 points).
- Minimum pass threshold: 80/100 to proceed to ramp.

Prelaunch checklist (short actionable items):
- [ ] Runbook published and reviewed (link to doc) - owner: Leah
- [ ] Oncall rota populated for T-72h to T+48h - owner: Product-ops
- [ ] Pager tests executed for all oncall entries - owner: SRE
- [ ] Canary traffic profile scripted and verified - owner: Release eng
- [ ] Synthetic checks created (end-to-end smoke) - owner: QA
- [ ] Telemetry alerts set and smoke alerts validated - owner: Observability
- [ ] Customer comm templates drafted (for partial rollback & full rollback) - owner: CS
- [ ] Rollback path dry-run (<3m) - owner: Release lead

Launch-day quick commands (ops cheatsheet):
- Feature-flag route set: /ffctl set model-rollout new-model 20% --env=prod
- Re-route to previous variant: /ffctl set model-rollout new-model 0% && /ffctl set model-rollout prev-model 100%
- Emergency throttling: /trafficctl throttle global --percent=30
- Kill model fleet (last resort): infra command (see infra-runbook link)

Owner action items (short horizon):
- Marco: add cost-per-1k token metric to primary dashboard and wire notify threshold (due: 2026-02-20).
- Aisha: finalize oncall rota and test paging for two backups (due: 2026-02-18).
- Diego: run a model-behavior smoke with 1k synthetic prompts to validate output stability (due: 2026-02-19).
- Leah: run T-72h dry run and capture gaps, publish final runbook (due: 2026-02-22).

Open questions / topics for next sync:
- What is the exact baseline definition for cost-per-1k tokens? (infra-only or infra+license?) Need finance input (JIRA: FIN-213).
- Do we want automated traffic rollback after a single hard threshold breach (yes/no)? Tradeoff: faster rollback vs potential false positives.
- Should we include a customer-facing status ping automation when p95 latency crosses SLO for >30m? Ops + CS to discuss.

References & links:
- Incident template: https://confluence.redwood/INCIDENT-TEMPLATE
- Infra rollback playbook: https://confluence.redwood/infra/rollback
- Feature-flag controller docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ffctl#readme

Notes to self (rough):
- This doc is intentionally short. Keep the telemetry minimal and actionable. Avoid 20+ widgets that nobody watches.
- Prioritize oncall fatigue reduction: pre-assign backups and have a 15-min warm handover for any long incidents.
Revision history:
- 2026-02-12: initial draft by Leah Thompson.
- 2026-02-20: added cost metric and alert thresholds (Marco).
- 2026-03-01: clarified rollback timing and updated owner list (Leah).

End of doc.
